newsitem.title: UK: UK budget delay shifts LIFFE pit trade to APT.
newsitem.headline: UK budget delay shifts LIFFE pit trade to APT.

text.p: A delay to the British budget means most futures market reaction will occur in automated trading rather than through open outcry, traders at LIFFE said on Wednesday.
British finance minister Gordon Brown's budget speech will be delayed by up to half an hour from the planned 1430 GMT start time, the Treasury said.
A Treasury spokesman said the delay was caused by a parliamentary question from a Conservative member about an alleged leak of information about private medical insurance.

A spokesman for LIFFE, the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange, said it was too late for the exchange to make further alterations to the floor and automated pit trading (APT) times for British equity and interest rate contracts.

A LIFFE official said most market reaction to the budget would probably take place in Thursday's open outcry session. But some traders said there would be an exodus from the floor to APT to allow trade to continue during the budget speech.
APT posted a record turnover of 95,654 contracts on June 21, 1997. That compares with average daily volume on LIFFE of 811,642, according to figures for June 1997.
